backlogged.summary: When the recovery's merge of integration into the feature worktree itself conflicts (integration moved after the failed post-merge verify), the feature is blocked as post_merge_verify with 'automatic post-merge verify recovery failed: cannot merge …'. The SPEC only says a conflict after the recovery's re-merge is merge_conflict and does not cover this case.

e.conflictTried is no longer written anywhere; it is read only for the pre-F32 state-file migration in runOne. The migration line is the only remaining user, so the field name lingers in state validation and docs.

failedTestNames trims leading whitespace before matching '✖ ' / 'not ok ', so indented nested failures count. This is broader than the contract's literal 'lines starting with'; it is documented in SPEC §6.1 and docs/run.md but is a deliberate extension.
flaky_tests names come from raw command output and are not passed through the env-value redactor before they go into the verdict and the run report, unlike verify_failures messages.

flaky_tests names are copied from the first run's raw stdout/stderr into the verify result, the verdict file and the run report without the env redactor that verify_failures uses. A test name that contains an env secret value (for example a parametrized test title) would appear unredacted.

recoverPostMerge passes the result of revParse(refs/heads/<integration>) straight to merge-base/merge without a null check. This is the same unclear-failure pattern as B165, now in the post-merge recovery path.
The blocked post_merge_verify detail still includes v.error unredacted (B197). The new recovery path appends to that detail without redacting it.

The recovery fail() path does not check the result of `git merge --abort` in the feature worktree, so a failed abort leaves the worktree mid-merge and the blocked detail does not say so. This mirrors B172 for resolveConflict.
